clue.text: Soft mineral discovered in Emmental cheese

indicators.note: discovered in says the answer is found sitting inside the words that follow, running across the join

explanation.surface: A geologist finds a soft mineral buried in a block of Swiss cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered in' points to the letters spanning the end of 'Emmental' and the start of 'cheese'.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale.

clue.text: Knott, we hear, needs a spell in the old game

definitions.text: needs a spell in the old game

explanation.surface: Someone named Knott needs a turn in an old-fashioned game.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname Knott sounds like 'knot', a gnarl in wood, which is one sense of the answer; 'knur and spell' is an old northern English game where a ball (the knur) is struck from a sprung trap (the spell).
explanation.definitionFit: A knur is a hard knot in timber, and also the wooden ball partnered by the spell in the old pub game of knur and spell.

clue.text: Actual existence, whichever way we look at it

indicators.text: whichever way we look at it
indicators.note: whichever way we look at it says the word reads the same from either end

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A philosopher insists that real existence is the same however you view it.
explanation.definitionFit: Esse is the Latin-derived philosophical term for being, actual existence.

clue.text: Met Bedi spinning-that's when he retired

indicators.note: spinning, the bowler's craft here, says the letters of the two words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Batsmen meet the spin bowler Bedi and are soon out and back in the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishan Bedi was an Indian spin bowler, so 'spinning' and 'retired' read as cricket; 'retired' really means went to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night happens at the hour set for going to sleep.

clue.text: Wilde's Lady of the Lake?

parts.note: Oscar Wilde wrote a comedy about a Lady whose title is also the name of the largest lake in England's Lake District

explanation.surface: A question about which of Oscar Wilde's heroines might rule a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady of the Lake is Arthurian, but here she is Wilde's Lady from 'Lady ___'s Fan', named after a lake in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Windermere's Fan is Wilde's play, and Windermere is England's largest natural lake.

clue.text: A nastiness dispelled by French composer

indicators.note: dispelled says the letters of the nasty phrase are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: A composer from France banishes all unpleasantness with his music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispelled' scatters A NASTINESS into the name of Camille Saint-Saëns, composer of The Carnival of the Animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Saint-Saëns was a nineteenth-century composer born in Paris.

clue.text: Sunday newspaper producers who go full speed ahead

parts.note: printers produce newspapers on their presses

explanation.surface: Those who print the Sunday papers race to get them out on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners who race short distances at maximum pace go flat out.

clue.text: Security at court for bachelor, one approaching fifty

indicators.note: approaching says the next piece comes right up beside the one before

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A court sets the security for a single man who is nearly fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bail is money pledged to a court as a guarantee that a released accused will return.

clue.text: Drink, chilled, to go with the game?

explanation.surface: A cold drink to go with a game of shuttlecock.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton cup is an old iced summer drink of claret, soda and sugar, named after the Duke of Beaufort's house; the house also gave its name to the racket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton cup is a chilled claret punch, and the name is also the shuttlecock-and-racket sport.

clue.text: He guides the plane when president carries writer

indicators.note: carries says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a US president
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A pilot guides the aircraft while the president travels with an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft and a pilot; it is the woodworker's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker smooths timber by pushing a plane over it.

clue.text: Plymouth has no opening for a strand

indicators.note: has no says a part is taken away from the place name

parts.note: a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: Plymouth lacks a harbour entrance for a stretch of coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strand' suggests a beach to go with Plymouth; it is a single thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A ply is one strand twisted into yarn or rope.

clue.text: Father's little love-a bit of skirting

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
O is love, the zero score in tennis, and it is a single small letter

explanation.surface: A father's small affection for a piece of skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirting' suggests a girlfriend; it is skirting board on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower band of an interior wall, a decorative strip like a skirting board.

clue.text: Theory held by numismatist

indicators.note: held by says the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A coin collector clings to a theory.
explanation.definitionFit: An -ism is a doctrine or system of belief.

clue.text: She's a trying type

parts.note: trying here means judging a case in court, so this is a woman who tries a defendant

explanation.surface: A tiresome woman who tests everyone's patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' reads as irritating, but a court tries a case and she sits on its panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A female member of a jury helps decide a trial's verdict.

clue.text: Kipling's game forest and reserve

parts.note: a jungle is a dense forest full of wild game
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Kipling hunts in a forest set aside as a game reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game reserve' looks like one phrase; 'game' joins 'forest' and 'reserve' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungle Book is Rudyard Kipling's collection of stories about Mowgli.

clue.text: Stripy apple obtained from dark trees?

indicators.note: obtained from says the letters are taken from the two words and reworked

explanation.surface: A streaked apple picked from shadowy trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained from' reorders DARK TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Redstreak is an old English cider apple with red-striped skin.

clue.text: Oriel, perhaps, with shrub in smallest of gardens

parts.note: an oriel is one kind of bay window
box is an evergreen shrub used for hedging

explanation.surface: A bay window with a shrub, the tiniest of gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is also an Oxford college, a possible distraction; here it is a projecting upper-floor window.
explanation.definitionFit: A planter on a sill holds flowers, a garden in miniature.

clue.text: in the matter of legal business

definitions.text: in the matter of legal business

parts.words: in the matter of legal business
parts.note: a Latin phrase meaning concerning, used in the titles of legal cases

explanation.surface: A phrase about the subject of a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is Latin for concerning, used to head court cases and formal letters.

clue.text: Done any mixing of painkiller?

indicators.note: mixing of says the letters of the words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A pharmacist asks whether any analgesic has been compounded yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing of' reorders DONE ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a drug that relieves pain.

clue.text: First topic we hear, infer mally, about?

definitions.text: First topic we hear, infer mally, about?

indicators.note: about says the collected letters are turned around into a new order
First says only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: What do we first hear people chat about casually?
explanation.walkthrough: 'infer mally' is the scan splitting 'informally'. 'First' takes T from 'topic', and 'about' rearranges it with WE and HEAR; the whole clue describes the British habit of opening small talk with the forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions outdoors are the classic opening subject of casual British conversation.

clue.text: Sense and Sensibility?

parts.note: the novel title is read as two nouns that each mean emotional awareness or the faculty of touch

explanation.surface: A question about Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The title is Austen's novel, but read as two plain nouns both are one word: a sense such as touch, and sensibility as emotional response.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch is one of the senses, and emotional sensitivity is sensibility; one word covers both.

clue.text: Musical character in uniform

explanation.surface: A character in a musical wearing a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical character' suggests a role in a show; it is a written symbol in music notation.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat sign lowers a note by a semitone, and a flat rate or surface is even and uniform.

clue.text: Homage one C. Basie arranged

indicators.note: arranged, as a jazz chart is arranged, says the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A tribute that one Count Basie orchestrated.
explanation.walkthrough: Count Basie was a jazz bandleader, so 'arranged' reads as music; it reorders ONE C BASIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of deference or respect, such as a bow.

clue.text: A party difficulty

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A celebration that turns out to be trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, trouble in getting something done.

clue.text: Fighting in retirement is not refined

indicators.note: in retirement says the word is withdrawn, so it is read going back

parts.note: war is fighting

explanation.surface: A retired boxer is a bit rough around the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw materials are crude and unprocessed.

clue.text: Blow it t-expression used to scare kids in Old English

indicators.note: in says the scaring word goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: bo is an exclamation to startle, as in being unable to say bo to a goose

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned shout to frighten children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow it' reads as a mild curse; it is something you blow, a woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is played by blowing through its double reed.

clue.text: Modern writer in global issue

parts.note: a globe is a ball shape
a point is an issue under discussion

explanation.surface: A contemporary author takes part in a worldwide debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests a person; it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a rolling metal tip came into wide use in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Church-warden is a sort to speak in high voice

explanation.surface: A parish official is the kind to talk in a squeaky voice.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a parish officer, but also a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden is a long clay smoking pipe, and to pipe is to speak shrilly.

clue.text: Part of mosaic on religious theme?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a mosaic depicts a religious subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a holy image, often of Christ or a saint.

clue.text: One of two to succeed on time

indicators.note: on says the second piece follows on from the first

parts.note: to win is to succeed

explanation.surface: One of a pair managing to succeed in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is either of two children born together.

clue.text: Wine or pop?

explanation.surface: A choice between wine and a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' suggests soda; in British slang to pop something is to pawn it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a German white wine, and to hock is to pawn, as pop means in British slang.

clue.text: A phone-box I find out of order-this keeps me at home

indicators.note: out of order, as a broken phone box is, says the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A broken phone box means I stay at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as the phone box being broken; it rearranges A PHONE BOX I.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and dislike of foreigners makes one reluctant to go abroad.
